title: Q3 Runway: Dedicated autoscale pilot roadmap, OKRs, and launch criteria
creator: Liam Rodriguez
description:
Goal: Define and approve the Q3 roadmap slice that launches a controlled customer pilot for Dedicated autoscaling (autoscale for reserved pools). This ticket captures scope, OKRs, success metrics, phased rollout plan, cross-team responsibilities, and launch gates.

Scope (what we will deliver in Q3 slice):
- Autoscale controller (policy engine) v1: scale-up/scale-down rules tied to queue latency and utilization thresholds.
- Integration with dedicated pool reservation billing for correct chargeback reporting.
- Console UX: pilot-only toggle, per-pool scaling metrics, and SLO dashboard widgets.
- Operator runbook: canary rollout playbook, rollback steps, incident contacts.
- Pilot onboarding template for 3 early customers.

OKRs (top-level):
- O: Validate autoscale improves reserved pool utilization and reduces manual ops burden.
  - KR1: Reduce average idle GPU hours across pilot pools by >= 30% in 30 days.
  - KR2: Achieve autoscale-triggered capacity adjustments within target latency (scale decision -> capacity change) <= 2 minutes 95% of the time.
  - KR3: Maintain customer-facing request latency P95 within 1.1x of baseline for 99.9% of requests during pilot.
  - KR4: Obtain successful pilot sign-off from at least 2 of 3 participating customers with documented SLA acceptance and billing clarity.

Success metrics / guardrails:
- Utilization uplift and idle hour reduction dashboards (linked).
- Autoscale action audit logs (every scale event must be recorded with reason).
- Safety constraints: never auto-evict running workloads; scale-down uses conservative cooling window of 15m by default.
- Cost delta analysis: per-customer cost-per-token objective to be within 10% of pre-pilot baselines or with documented customer consent.

Rollout phases and timeline (high-level):
- Phase 0 (Mar-Apr): Design + spike. Finalize policy thresholds, simulation harness, and billing mapping.
- Phase 1 (May-Jun): Internal dogfooding in staging with synthetic workloads and loadtests. Iterate on kernel scheduling and KV cache implications.
- Phase 2 (Jul-Aug): Select 3 pilot customers, enable pilot toggle in dedicated UI, monitor for 30d.
- Phase 3 (Sep): Consolidate findings, produce runbook and recommended default policies for GA decision.

Launch gates (required to enable pilot on a customer):
- Internal load tests pass for scale-up/scale-down correctness.
- Observability: pool-level metrics, action audit logs, SLO tracking dashboards present and scoped for customer.
- Billing: dedicated reservation mapping validated by finance and built into billing pipeline.
- Legal & Security: security review completed (ticket attached) and customer contract addendum template approved.

Stakeholders and responsibilities:
- Product (Aisha): overall scope, customer communications, pilot success evaluation.
- Eng - Serving runtime (owner ENG-21012): autoscale controller implementation and kernel scheduling validation.
- Eng - Billing (owner ENG-33244): billing integration and chargeback tests.
- SRE/Infra: canary rollout orchestration, alerting and incident response.
- DevRel/SE: pilot onboarding and customer guidance.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Aggressive scale-down causes cold starts and customer-perceived latency spikes. Mitigation: conservative default cooldown and warm pool of minimum fraction of capacity.
- Risk: Billing mismatch for reserved vs burst capacity. Mitigation: end-to-end billing test with finance before any customer pilot.
- Risk: Autoscale interacts poorly with KV cache affinity. Mitigation: enforce cache-aware pod placement in initial rollout; focus on model variants with stateless caching for pilot customers.

Acceptance criteria (for this ticket):
1) Roadmap and milestones agreed by Eng, SRE, Billing, Legal, and Sales.
2) Pilot onboarding checklist and customer contract addendum drafted.
3) Observable success metrics and dashboards created and validated in staging.
4) Risk mitigations documented and runbook drafted.
